data.text: Good, I can see the structure. Now I'll run a SQL query to calculate the average number of items per order, filtering out canceled and unavailable orders as per the business glossary.

args.purpose: Calculate average number of items per order (excluding canceled/unavailable orders)
args.sql:
SELECT 
    COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id) AS total_orders,
    SUM(1) AS total_items,
    AVG(COUNT(*)) OVER () AS avg_items_per_order
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
GROUP BY oi.order_id

data.text: The query returned many rows with the same average. Let me run a simpler aggregated query to get just the single average value.

args.purpose: Calculate average number of items per order (excluding canceled/unavailable orders)
args.sql:
SELECT 
    COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id) AS total_orders,
    SUM(1) AS total_items,
    CAST(SUM(1) AS DOUBLE) / COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id) AS avg_items_per_order
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
